messages:
deploy-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT: /v1/generate p99 latency spike on continuous-batching path (>2.5s) detected by canary. Affected region: us-west-2. Auto-escalation: paging oncall.
miguel: oncall here, looking. which customers? any 5xxs?
deploy-bot: no elevated 5xxs, increased timeouts from streaming clients, spike started ~1744999800, now ongoing. grafana: https://grafana.company/r/contbatch-p99 (internal)
jen: digging into traces — streaming stalls correlate with large batch sizes where one request has seq_len > 1200. p95 ~ 320ms, p99 ~ 2.6s. p999 tails up to ~6s for some streams.
ryan: ack. this smells like HOB (head-of-line) blocking from mixed sequence lengths in the continuous batcher.
miguel: can we apply quick mitigation? reduce max_batch_size or isolate long-seq requests to separate lane?
jen: yes. two quick mitigations: 1) reduce max_batch_size from 128->32 on contbatch scheduler; 2) enable seqlen-aware sharding (experimental flag) to isolate >512 token requests into separate queue. both low-risk.
ryan: i'm +1 for reducing max_batch_size immediately, then enable seqlen sharding if we see improvement.
infra-bot: @miguel rolling configuration change: contbatch.max_batch_size=32 for pool=prod-usw2. Rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Command: `infractl rollout-config --service=contbatch --key=max_batch_size --value=32 --strategy=gradual --steps=5,25,100`
miguel: starting rollout at 1745000060. monitoring p99 and streaming error rate.
jen: added a temporary qos rule to prefer requests flagged streaming=false to faster path. This will divert non-streaming short requests.
ryan: logs show backlog on queue shard #3 where long sequences accumulate. attaching sample trace snippet:

```
TRACE ID: abc123
queue_wait_ms: 1800
batch_size: 96
max_seq_len_in_batch: 1800
processing_ms: 30
streaming_stall: true
```
miguel: after first 25% step (1745000120) p99 dropped to 1.1s, streaming stalls decreased noticeably. continuing rollout.
jen: customer impact estimate: ~3.8% of total requests hit the long-seq path; of those ~45% saw degraded streaming (stalls/timeouts). top affected customers: internal-ci, partner-eval (non-critical but noisy).
sre-lead: good data. we should still open an incident ticket (INC-2026-1745) and link postmortem. please capture timeline and config diffs.
ryan: suggest followups: - make seqlen-aware scheduling default for prod; - add adaptive smaller-batch fallback when variance in seq_len > threshold; - add metric: fraction of batches with max_seq_len > 4x median.
jen: created a short-lived canary test to replay mixed-seqlen traffic with current config. running now (1745000300). also kicking KV cache eviction on a few nodes to avoid kv-growth impact on batching code: `redis-cli -h kv-prod-5 EVAL "redis.call('FLUSHDB')" 0` (will limit to canary nodes only).
miguel: rollout at 100% complete at 1745000360. p99 stabilized ~420ms, p95 ~ 270ms. streaming stalls back to baseline in metrics, continuing to monitor for 30m.
infra-bot: rollback window 1 hour. If any regression, use `infractl rollback-config --service=contbatch --key=max_batch_size`.
jen: handoff to miguel for post-incident follow-ups: root cause likely mixed sequence-lengths causing unfair scheduling + excessive batching that amplified single long request. mitigation: smaller batches + seqlen sharding helped.
miguel: taking post-incident. will file P0 action items: 1) run traffic replay with mixed seqlen distributions and validate adaptive batching; 2) implement seqlen-aware default policy and gradual rollout plan; 3) add alert for fraction_of_batches_with_max_seq_gt_4x_median > 1%.
sre-lead: please include customer impact numbers, rollout timestamps, and config diffs in the incident doc. nice quick mitigation team. :thumbsup:
miguel: thanks all — closing handoff at 1745000420. I'll update INC-2026-1745 and ping when postmortem is ready.
